regimens.indication: Short-Term Inotropic Support in Cardiac Decompensation / Septic Cardiomyopathy (Adults — Continuous IV)

refs.quote: Dobutamine in 5% Dextrose Injection, USP is indicated when parenteral therapy is necessary for inotropic support in the short-term treatment of patients with cardiac decompensation due to depressed contractility resulting either from organic heart disease or from cardiac surgical procedures.

For adults with septic shock and cardiac dysfunction with persistent hypoperfusion despite adequate volume status and arterial blood pressure, suggest either adding dobutamine to norepinephrine or using epinephrine alone. regimens.dose_text: Start at 0.5 to 1.0 mcg/kg/min (usual clinical range 2 to 20 mcg/kg/min, max 40 mcg/kg/min) continuous IV infusion via calibrated pump; titrate every few minutes based on cardiac output, BP, heart rate, ectopy, and urine output. Often combined with norepinephrine if vasodilatory hypotension coexists.

renal_basis.note: No renal adjustment required; short plasma half-life ~2 minutes

hepatic.note: No hepatic dose-adjustment bands specified in labeling

refs.quote: Dobutamine is a direct-acting inotropic agent whose primary activity results from stimulation of the β-receptors of the heart while producing comparatively mild chronotropic, hypertensive, arrhythmogenic, and vasodilative effects. It does not cause the release of endogenous norepinephrine, as does dopamine.

tier.note: 5-axis synthesis: Animal reproduction studies in rats/rabbits showed no fetal harm, but adequate human pregnancy studies are lacking; reserve for clear maternal cardiac decompensation.

refs.quote: Reproduction studies performed in rats and rabbits have revealed no evidence of harm to the fetus due to dobutamine. The drug, however, has not been administered to pregnant women and should be used only when the expected benefits clearly outweigh the potential risks to the fetus.

pregnancy_pk.value: No formal pregnancy PK adjustment; titrate to maternal hemodynamic/cardiac output response.

Pediatric Use: Dobutamine has been shown to increase cardiac output and systemic pressure in pediatric patients of every age group.

postpartum.value: Standard ICU hemodynamic tapering applies postpartum (e.g., peripartum cardiomyopathy).

refs.quote: Following delivery, standard adult ICU vasopressor titration applies with close monitoring for postpartum hemorrhage, cardiomyopathy, or pre-eclampsia overlap; no routine postpartum dose-reduction schedule is required beyond standard hemodynamic weaning.
No data are available on the excretion of dobutamine into human milk.

lactation_summary.value: Dobutamine is inactive orally and has a ~2 minute plasma half-life; clinically significant infant exposure via breastmilk is not expected.

refs.quote: Because dobutamine is poorly absorbed orally and has an extremely short plasma half-life, clinically significant exposure in a breastfed infant is not expected.
